cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.

mechanism: A claims a pupil learned its method and uses that supposed near-mastery to convert holding stems into completing the bouquet.
confusable: The teacher-like correction motivates doing the next small step, rather than giving an unrelated lecture or assigning the entire task at once.
comparison: Shelf under a work deadline versus collaborative craft finishing driven by B useful corrections.
seedUse: Canonical D25 bouquet wire/sharp-end chain already fits taught craft and S05 appropriation of a pupil correct suggestion; retain the original if rereading supports it.
